recommendation: Keep the audit commit unless someone with Jira attachment access can recover Archive.zip. If recovered, compare the OO QA report entries against current build-scoped OO source and create precise follow-up fixes only for remaining substantive discrepancies.
issue_request: FHIR-17607 is a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction for the Orders and Observations work group. It asked editors to use the attached Archive.zip QA review files from an earlier QA process to check that updates had been applied; Jira records an Auto-approved resolution, related page FHIR-core-many, applied-for version R5, and no comments.
initial_application: No current source reference, git commit message, or history search before this AutoFHIR run explicitly mentions FHIR-17607, GF#17607, or #17607. Late-2018 Orders and Observations QA-related commits changed DiagnosticReport, Specimen, BodyStructure, Device, SpecimenDefinition, and related source, but none tie those changes to the FHIR-17607 archive contents or prove every archive item is satisfied.
additional_context: Attachment 15603 is the only apparent detailed source of requested changes, and both secure and REST download attempts returned HTTP 403. source/fhir.ini lists active OO-owned artifacts, and checked-in qa/*.docx review documents exist, but no active build reference to those QA archives was found. Sibling QA report issues have separate work-group scopes and attachments, and community searches found no direct FHIR-17607 discussion or minutes clarifying the archive contents.
reconciliation: No source file was changed. The combined branch now contains an empty human-review audit commit documenting that source changes would be speculative without the archive contents.
